summary: Working in Indology and philosophy, Gopikamohan Bhattacharya studied under Erich Frauwallner. He later held a post at Kurukshetra University, attested in 1977.

Gopinath Kaviraj was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at University Maharani College and University of Allahabad under Madhusudan Ojha, Shashadhar Tarkachuramani, and Arthur Venis, he held leadership roles at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi.

Gordon Charles Roadarmel worked in Indology after studying at Woodstock School, College of Wooster, University of Allahabad, Chicago Theological Seminary, and UC Berkeley. He taught Hindi at the University of Chicago (1963–1965) and was an assistant professor at UC Berkeley (~1969–1972).

Gordon Dester Kaufman was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Bethel College, Northwestern, Yale, and Yale Divinity School. He held posts at Pomona College, Vanderbilt University, and Harvard University, where he became Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity in 1963.

Gordon H. Fairbanks worked in linguistics and Indology, earning degrees from Mount Royal, Alberta, and Wisconsin-Madison. His career included posts at Southwestern University, Cornell University (1945–1970), Deccan College, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

Working in history, archaeology, sinology, and linguistics, Gordon Hannington Luce studied at Dean Close School, Emmanuel College, and the University of Cambridge. He subsequently served as a professor at the University of Rangoon from approximately 1912 to 1964.

Gordon Johnson is an Indology and history scholar who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as a fellow of Trinity and Selwyn Colleges, President of Wolfson College, Deputy Vice-Chancellor of Cambridge University, and President of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Gordon Matthews specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying at Merton College and Mansfield College. He served as Professor of English and Vice-Principal at Madras Christian College (~1912–1939) before becoming a Lecturer in Tamil at SOAS University of London in 1939.

Gore Ouseley was active in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as linguistics. He served at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (~1810–1815) and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1844).

Gottfried Bernhardy was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and the Humboldt University of Berlin before holding a long-term academic post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from around 1829 to 1875.

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at Academic Gymnasium Danzig and under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen, he held posts at Vilnius University (~1798–1803) and the Imperial University of Vilna (~1803–1824).

Gottfried Hartmann Weigle worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren and under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Tübingen, later serving as a missionary for the Basel Mission starting in 1838.

Gottfried Hermann was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Jena and the University of Leipzig. At Leipzig, he served as professor of philosophy from 1798 and director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.

Gottfried Kinkel was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at the University of Bonn (~1831–1834). He later held academic appointments at the University of Bonn (~1837–1848) and ETH Zurich (~1866–1882).
Gottlieb L. Schaenzlin was an Indology scholar who earned his M.A. from Johns Hopkins University by 1921. Earlier in his career, he served as Principal of the Collins Institute in 1914.

Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology who studied under Christoph Theodosius Walther at the University of Königsberg. He held posts at the University of Königsberg and later served as professor at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences.

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner was a scholar of linguistics and Asian studies who studied at King's College London, Freiburg, and Heidelberg. He served as Principal of Oriental College and Government College, Lahore, and founded the Oriental Institute, Woking.

Gouriswar Bhattacharya worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Calcutta and University of Basel under Alfred Bloch, he held posts at Visva-Bharati University, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the Free University of Berlin.

Govind Chandra Pande was an Indologist and historian who studied under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad and University of Rajasthan, Chairman of the Allahabad Museum, and Chairman of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

Govind Kumar Meena is an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya and Banaras Hindu University. In 2022, he became an assistant professor at Government College University, Lahore.
